To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GW signals from core-collapse supernova explosions can be used to determine the explosion mechanism, that our method is capable of distinguishing between the most promising explosion mechanisms, and that the most distant core-collapse supernovas that can be distinguished are those that occur within the Milky Way.

we have developed a method for determining the mechanism driving core-collapse supernovas from GW signals that may be observed by Advanced LIGO, that our method is capable of distinguishing the neutrino, acoustic, and magnetorotational explosion mechanisms, and that it is capable of distinguishing between models of accretion-induced and iron core-collapse supernovæ.

(i) GWs from core-collapse supernova explosions can provide a unique probe of the explosion mechanism, (ii) our method is able to distinguish between different explosion mechanisms, and (iii) our method can differentiate between models of rotating accretion induced collapse and models of rotating core-collapse supernovas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection, characterization, and identification of GW signals from core-collapse supernova explosions, and the use of these signals to probe the physics of these explosions.
the question, what can we infer about the core-collapse supernova mechanism from gravitational-wave observations?

the development of a promising method for identifying the explosion mechanism of core-collapse supernova events that produce GW signals, and we show that our method is capable of distinguishing between different explosion mechanisms at a distance that is relevant to the detection of core-collapse supernovea with the next generation of ground-based GW observatories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can distinguish magnetorotationally driven explosions and iron core collapse out to several kpcs.
we can determine the most likely explosion mechanisms underlying GW bursts with a precision of 10%–30% in distance.
we can distinguish between all models for the most energetic core-collapse supernovas out to a few kpc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the method described in this work is capable of distinguishing between different core-collapse supernova mechanisms out to a few kpc, and is thus capable of providing a new and independent way of probing supernova explosions in the Galaxy.
the GW signal of the explosion of a core-collapse SN can be used to determine the explosion mechanism and to distinguish different progenitor scenarios.
we can identify the explosion mechanism with a probability of 90% out to 2  kPC and a probability of 50% out to 4  kPc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GWs emitted by core-collapse supernovas can be used to infer the underlying explosion mechanism and thus provide new insight into the physics of stellar death.
GWs from core-collapse supernova explosions can be used to infer the underlying explosion mechanism, even if the signal is detected by a single detector.
GWs from core-collapse supernova explosions may provide a powerful new way to determine the explosion mechanism of these important astrophysical transients, which is currently uncertain.
